CS 431

Cyber-Physical Systems

  • Undergraduate
  • 3 credits

Offered: Spring 2026, Spring 2025, Spring 2024

Students study computing and communication in systems that interact with the physical world. Using examples such as connected devices, smart grids, and autonomous vehicles, they learn to model, simulate, and verify cyber-physical systems.

Selected Topics

  • Cyber-physical systems and the Internet of Things
  • Mathematical modeling and simulation
  • Analysis, testing, and verification
  • Automatic synthesis and control

Learning Objectives

  • Model and simulate basic cyber-physical systems.
  • Compare approaches to analysis, testing, and verification.
  • Explain the role of synthesis and control in cyber-physical systems design.

Coursework & Projects

Students complete an applied project, a short written report, and a virtual poster that describes the motivation, approach, and results.

Related Course

  • CS 531 · Security in Cyber-Physical Systems
